files_reviewed: .env.local.example (key names only; values are blank placeholders except a placeholder base URL)
README.md (security and architecture sections, grep for the rest)
note: No committed .env and no secret in client code. All model calls (Cognee recall, Groq router) run on the server. Storage is Upstash Redis reached only from the server, so there are no database_rules labels. Webhook delivery has a strong SSRF guard: https only, check at connect time, no redirects, HMAC signature. Actions start disabled and every API route under /api/companies checks membership. Stale comments in actions.ts 319-320, webhook.ts 1-2 and the actions and test routes still say the dashboard has no auth. The docs page offers a Forget API for backend use, but the route needs a signed-in browser session. globals.css not reviewed (styles only). | Second labeler: Next.js app on Cognee Cloud (answers and memory) with a Groq router that picks one configured webhook action per turn. No SQL database: Upstash Redis and one shared Cognee tenant, both used server-side only. No model call or model key in browser code. No committed secrets. Real controls exist: Google sign-in plus per-route membership checks on /api/companies/*, SSRF checks on webhooks at connect time, HMAC-signed payloads, action caps (5 per customer per hour, 100 per company per day), a 60 s dedupe, at most one tool call per turn, and server-side re-validation of tool args by type. The main gaps are customer identity taken from the request body, cross-company session reads through the shared tenant, no rate limit on the public chat endpoint, and model-fired webhooks with no confirmation step.

labels.what: maybeFireAction posts the company webhook (refund tickets, escalations, any configured action) straight from the Groq tool call in the same chat turn. No customer confirm step and no staff approval before the fire

Router prompt says to take parameter values only from the customer's message and never invent them. validateArgs only checks type, required and length (500 chars, abs 1e15). Nothing checks that a value such as order_id appears in the message. README and landing FAQ repeat the claim

Router prompt says the customer message, agent answer and history are data, never instructions. Code pastes all three, including stored memory text that holds earlier customer messages, into one user message with no escaping or separation check

Router prompt says to call a tool only on a clear match and call nothing when in doubt. Code fires the first tool call the model returns. There is no confidence check, and the grounded flag is only passed to the prompt, never checked

Default system prompt says to answer only from context and never invent order numbers, dates or events. Code only runs a refusal regex. pickAnswer keeps the longest non-refusal answer, and grounded=true means only that it was not a refusal. The API reports this flag to callers as grounded

Model-filled action params get type and length checks only. Number fields accept up to 1e15 with no per-field min, max or allowed values, so a refund amount is unbounded. The 5-per-hour per-customer cap keys on the client-chosen customerId, so changing visitorId bypasses it. Only the 100-per-day company cap holds

Public chat API trusts client-supplied visitorId and email. customerId is a hash of the email, so anyone with the published public key can send a victim's email, get that customer's history recalled into answers, and fire actions whose payload carries the victim's identity

Conversation list is the tenant-wide Cognee session list filtered by the prefix everdesk-<slug>-. A slug like acme also matches sessions of acme-cloud, so one company's members see another company's conversations. The overview page uses the same prefix filter

Conversation detail loads any Cognee session by id and never checks that the id belongs to this slug. A signed-in member of any company can read another company's transcript by changing the id in the URL
Feedback route checks membership of the slug but writes feedback to any sessionId and qaId from the body, with no check that the session belongs to that company
Client-supplied sessionId is accepted when it starts with everdesk-<slug>-. A caller can attach to another customer's session, or to a session of a company whose slug starts with the same prefix

Workspace membership is checked only in the layout. The pages under it (customers list with emails, settings with members, actions, conversations, overview) load data with no check of their own, and proxy.ts only checks sign-in. Next.js does not re-run a layout on partial renders

Public CORS-open chat endpoint has no rate limit per IP or visitor. Each turn runs a paid Cognee LLM recall, and each grounded turn starts a durable cognify pipeline (agent.ts 291-311), against the findings doc plan of one write per conversation. Each call adds a KV visitor record. One caller can also use up the shared global Groq budget (10000 per day) for every company

Training URL fetch checks the host's DNS once, then fetches with redirect follow. A public URL that redirects to an internal or metadata address is not re-checked. DNS rebinding is also open, and the blocklist misses 100.64/10 and several IPv6 forms. Fetched text goes into the knowledge base and can be read back through chat. Any Google user can create a company and call this

Customer history is pulled from one shared memory dataset by a substring match on customerId. Raw customer messages are stored verbatim (line 294). A message that names another customer's id lands in that customer's history, which goes into their system prompt (lines 249-256): a stored cross-customer prompt injection
Answer path joins the raw customer message and the unvalidated client email (customerPrefix) into the recall query, and memory history into the system prompt, with no injection guard

Forget hard-deletes every memory item whose filename contains the URL id as a substring. The id is not validated, so an id like cust_ or txt deletes every customer's memory. Any member can do it, not only the owner
Access-Control-Allow-Origin * on the chat API. This is intended for the publishable key, but with no rate limits any site can drive paid calls

Overview shows tenant-wide Cognee sessionStats as Workspace spend and Tokens processed to every company, which leaks totals across tenants. It also takes only the last 200 tenant-wide sessions before filtering

Any signed-in Google user can create unlimited companies, each with two Cognee datasets and an agent. The train route has no file size, file type or text length limit and starts a cognify run each call
Sets feedback sent before the request. A non-2xx response is ignored (only a network error resets), so the UI shows success when the server rejected the feedback
Shows Training complete, your agent knows this now, whenever the training flag is false. The GET returns an errored flag that the panel never reads, so a failed build also shows success
Polls 60 times at 4 s. If the build has not finished after 4 minutes, it marks the step done anyway and shows Your support agent is live and trained (lines 207-214)

Says the agent provably knows nothing after forget. The route deletes only memory items whose filename matches. Cognee session transcripts for the customer, KB resolutions or skills that quote them, and ops events stay
Hardcoded event lines with fixed customer ids loop in a feed with a pulsing live dot on the landing page (lines 275-289). A comment says they come from a real session

Action and router caps (5 per customer per hour, 100 per company per day, 500 and 10000 router calls, 10 config writes) are code constants. The same numbers are typed again as prose in docs/page.tsx 209-210 and README 151-152, so they can drift
Groq URL, primary and fallback model names, 4 s timeout and 500-char param cap hardcoded
Production domain everdesk.allensaji.dev hardcoded here and in settings/page.tsx 23 (fallback host), docs/page.tsx, CodeTabs.tsx, webhook.ts 191 and fetch-docs.ts 88 user agents
Test script hardcodes http://localhost:3000 and slug zenith-test. It calls dashboard routes with no session, so it fails now that those routes need sign-in

The per-customer cap of 5 actions per hour is keyed on customerId, which comes from the client's visitorId or email. Rotating visitorId bypasses it. Only the 100-per-day company cap holds, and an attacker can use it up to block real customers' actions.
The whole response body is read into memory before the 2 MB size check runs.
Uploads have no size, count or type limit, and training (cognify, paid LLM processing) has no rate limit. Any signed-in Google user can create a company and start unlimited training runs.
visitorId (the only credential for an anonymous customer's memory) and the email are stored in localStorage, readable by any script on the widget origin.
/widget sends frame-ancestors *, so any site can frame the chat. This allows clickjacking of the email form and chat. It is intended for embedding.
customerId keeps only 8 hex chars (32 bits) of a sha256, so different customers can collide and share one memory history as the customer count grows.

The resolve form fills in the last customer question and answer by default, and submitting writes them into the shared knowledge base that every customer can retrieve. Customer-specific details can leak to other customers.

All companies share one Cognee tenant and API key. Sessions are not stored per company. Isolation is a session-id prefix filter in app code over the last 200 tenant-wide sessions. The README's isolated-per-company claim holds for datasets, not for sessions.

If listing the memory items fails, the error is swallowed as an empty list and the route still returns forgotten with 0 deleted. The UI then says the agent provably knows nothing. Session transcripts and knowledge-base resolutions that hold the customer's text are never deleted.

The chat route accepts messages up to 4000 chars, but the router truncates the message to 2000 chars. These are two different limits for the same value, so action params near the end of a long message never reach the router.
The client hardcodes the 10-field limit (params.length < 10) separately from MAX_PARAMS_PER_ACTION.
The embed snippet origin falls back to the hardcoded production domain everdesk.allensaji.dev.
Install snippets hardcode https://everdesk.allensaji.dev for the embed script, chat API and widget iframe.
Docs examples hardcode https://everdesk.allensaji.dev. The Forget API is documented for a company backend, but the route requires a dashboard Google session.

The company public key (pk_...) is sent from the browser and printed in the embed snippet. It is publishable by design, but it is the only gate on the chat endpoint that reads customer memory and fires actions.
